subject: Temporary tier upgrade + surge credits — launch support and rollback
messages:
From: Elena Moreno <elena.moreno@pulseworks.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Packaging options for launch — temporary uplift & rollback?

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the call earlier — PulseWorks is planning a product launch on Sept 15 and we expect a ~6x spike in inference volume for the first two weeks. We need a packaging option that lets us temporarily increase capacity without a long-term commitment, plus clear rollback (and credit) terms if volumes fall short.

Questions we have today:
- Can Redwood provide a time-limited tier upgrade (90 days max) and then auto-revert us back to our prior tier?
- How do surge credits (if any) work for burst traffic — are they applied as a buffer or as a prepaid top-up?
- If we commit to a short-term uplift, what discounting is available (especially if we hit usage thresholds)?
- What happens to add-on features (advanced caching, priority routing) during the temporary period — are they bundled or charged separately?

We'd like something that minimizes procurement friction. If you can send a simple three-option matrix (conservative / balanced / aggressive) with numbers and rollback mechanics, that would help our procurement and legal teams.

Attaching a short product forecast we used for planning.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Moreno
Head of Product Operations | PulseWorks
Attachments: forecast_q3_launch.csv (csv)
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Elena Moreno <elena.moreno@pulseworks.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-21T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options for launch — temporary uplift & rollback?

Elena — thanks for the clear ask and the forecast. Looping Ben (AE) and Priyom (legal/account ops) so we can put actionable options in front of procurement.

High-level: we can do a temporary tier upgrade plus optional surge credits. There are three ways customers typically structure this:
1) Temporary Tier Upgrade (timebox): upgrade to the next tier for a fixed window (30/60/90 days). Add-ons remain optional; pricing is prorated daily and we auto-revert at the end of the window.
2) Pay-as-you-burst with Surge Credits: keep your tier, buy surge credits as a buffer (applied only if actual usage exceeds baseline). Credits are consumed and there's a reconciliation after the period.
3) Hybrid (recommended for launches): temporary tier uplift coupled with a reserved surge credit pool—this limits cost volatility and gives you predictable headroom.

I'll ask Ben to sketch the numbers (3 scenarios) and include a rollback clause (auto-revert + unused-credit refund mechanics) so procurement has something to sign off on quickly.

Draft bundle options attached — Ben will follow up with a matrix and a draft MAF for legal.

Best,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
Attachments: bundle-options-v1.pdf (pdf)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Moreno <elena.moreno@pulseworks.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T08:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options for launch — temporary uplift & rollback?

Hi Elena — thanks for the forecast, that helps. I sketched three concrete options below using your expected peak (avg baseline -> 6x spike) and a 14-day launch window. Numbers are illustrative; we can tighten them once you confirm expected token throughput and concurrent QPS.

Option A — Conservative (low risk)
- Keep current tier; purchase 200k surge credits (prepaid buffer)
- No change in add-ons; advanced caching remains billed separately
- Credits consumed at normal per-token rate; unused credits refunded at 50% at end of period
- Estimated incremental cost: $12k for the window

Option B — Balanced (recommended)
- Temporary upgrade to next tier for 60 days (auto-revert)
- Reserved surge credit pool of 100k included
- Advanced caching bundled at 25% discount for the 60-day window
- If usage < 60% of reserved credits, apply a 30% refund on unused portion
- Estimated incremental cost: $28k pre-tax

Option C — Aggressive (high availability)
- Temporary upgrade two tiers for 90 days + priority routing add-on bundled
- Larger surge credit offset and an incentive discount ladder: 3% at $50k, 6% at $100k, 10% at $200k committed spend during the uplift window
- Full audit logs and expanded retention included as trial
- Estimated incremental cost: $72k with stepped discounts

Key notes / rollback mechanics:
- Auto-revert: we will schedule a revert to prior tier at the end of the timebox; a 7-day canary period preceding rollback allows for a controlled switch if you want to extend.
- Unused credit reconciliation: default refunds are prorated per the option rules above (we can negotiate higher refund % on larger commitments).
- Procurement docs: attached a draft MAF and a short proposal summary for internal review.

Next steps: please confirm (1) expected average and peak QPS, (2) whether you want add-ons bundled during the window, and (3) target approval timeline from procurement. Happy to hop on a quick call to review.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: MAF-draft.xlsx (spreadsheet), proposal-summary.pdf (pdf)
From: Elena Moreno <elena.moreno@pulseworks.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-24T10:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options for launch — temporary uplift & rollback?

Thanks Ben — this is exactly the level of detail procurement needs. Quick answers:
- Expected baseline: ~250 requests/minute (steady); projected peak: ~1,500 requests/minute for the two-week blast.
- Add-ons: we'd like advanced caching + priority routing included during the uplift if possible — reduces load and will improve latency for launch traffic.
- Procurement timeline: we need a signed MOU by Sept 1 to align with internal scheduling. Legal will push back on any language that looks like a non-refundable commitment.

A few clarifying questions:
1) The refund percentages on unused credits — are those firm or negotiable if we sign a longer (but still limited) commitment?
2) The canary window: can we have a 3-day read-only canary before auto-revert (logs-only, no traffic shift) plus a 7-day extension option we can exercise once?
3) For Option C discount ladder, can you do an early-spend accelerator — e.g., if we hit $50k in the first 10 days, you apply the next tier discount retroactively?

If you can update the MAF to reflect answers, we can route to procurement/legal next week.

—Elena
Elena Moreno
Head of Product Operations, PulseWorks
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Elena Moreno <elena.moreno@pulseworks.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-26T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options for launch — temporary uplift & rollback?

Elena — short answers and next steps below. Priyom copied for legal/accounting notes.

1) Refund % on unused credits: negotiable. Standard play is the tiers Ben listed; for a signed 90-day uplift we can increase the unused-credit refund to 70% for commitments > $50k. We'll mark that in the MAF as an optional concession.
2) Canary window: yes — we can do a 3-day read-only monitoring window (no traffic switch) followed by an automated 7-day extension option you can trigger. We'll add explicit language that the extension requires a one-email confirmation from your procurement contact to avoid operational delays.
3) Early-spend accelerator: we can support retroactive discounting if the $50k threshold is hit within the first 10 calendar days. We'll include a short clause for retroactive crediting of the higher discount level.

Action items I will own:
- Ben will update the numbers in the proposal (Option A/B/C) reflecting your QPS/peak.
- Priyom will add the canary/revert language and the revised refund ladder into the MAF.
- I'll send a condensed one-page summary for procurement to sign (MOU style) with a DocuSign link.

If that works, Ben — please update the attachment and we will circulate to procurement. Elena — if procurement can confirm the primary signer and their email, I'll include them on the DocuSign as the signee.

Best,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
Attachments: proposal-summary.pdf (updated)
